spec.commanderStyle: lean into what makes this commander unique

commander.name: Chatterfang, Squirrel General
commander.oracleText:
Forestwalk (This creature can't be blocked as long as defending player controls a Forest.)
If one or more tokens would be created under your control, those tokens plus that many 1/1 green Squirrel creature tokens are created instead.
{B}, Sacrifice X Squirrels: Target creature gets +X/-X until end of turn.

nonlands.name: Sol Ring
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: The strongest available generic acceleration, enabling early engines and a timely Chatterfang while leaving more mana for sacrifice activations.

nonlands.name: Arcane Signet
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Reliable two-mana fixing for both colors and for Chatterfang's black activation.

nonlands.name: Birds of Paradise
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: One-mana acceleration that fixes either color and remains useful as sacrifice fodder.

nonlands.name: Llanowar Elves
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Efficient turn-one green acceleration that can later be converted into cards, removal, or aristocrat triggers.

nonlands.name: Elves of Deep Shadow
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Provides the black mana needed for Chatterfang's activated ability and black aristocrats while costing only one mana.

nonlands.name: Sakura-Tribe Elder
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Fixes mana, guarantees a land through removal, and naturally supplies a creature death for the deck's payoffs.

nonlands.name: Nature's Lore
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Efficiently finds Forest duals and can establish both colors without adding a tapped land.

nonlands.name: Three Visits
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Redundant efficient Forest access that improves early Chatterfang and engine sequencing.

nonlands.name: Talisman of Resilience
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Dowsing Dagger requires an attack and successful transformation before producing mana. Talisman of Resilience provides immediate two-mana fixing and improves early Chatterfang, engine, and interaction sequencing.

nonlands.name: Chitterspitter
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: A commander-specific engine that continuously creates Squirrels while turning sacrificed tokens into a scalable anthem.

nonlands.name: Camellia, the Seedmiser
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Camellia is a stronger midgame token-conversion engine in this shell: Food sacrifices create additional Squirrels, and its forage ability provides a scalable anthem. It works especially well with Ygra, Academy Manufactor, and Tireless Provisioner.

nonlands.name: Academy Manufactor
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Turns every Clue, Food, or Treasure event into three artifact tokens, each of which also produces Chatterfang Squirrels.

nonlands.name: Tireless Provisioner
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Landfall produces either mana or life resources and becomes especially explosive when Manufactor and Chatterfang are present.

nonlands.name: Ophiomancer
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Creates a deathtouch Snake on each upkeep cycle and naturally supports instant-speed sacrifice interactions.

nonlands.name: Bitterblossom
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: An independent two-mana source of evasive bodies that steadily becomes a large Squirrel board with Chatterfang.

nonlands.name: Tireless Tracker
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Tireless Tracker repeatedly creates Clues from the deck's land drops, which become substantially more material with Academy Manufactor and Chatterfang, while also supplying reliable card advantage.

nonlands.name: Tendershoot Dryad
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Creates a token every upkeep and becomes a powerful secondary anthem once the deck reaches ten permanents.

nonlands.name: Viscera Seer
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: The best low-cost free outlet, allowing the deck to convert tokens into scry, death triggers, and protection from exile effects.

nonlands.name: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Carrion Feeder is a legitimate outlet but offers only growth. Yawgmoth is a repeatable sacrifice outlet that also draws cards, places -1/-1 counters for creature interaction, and proliferates, providing major role compression for the token-sacrifice plan.

nonlands.name: Yahenni, Undying Partisan
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Provides a repeatable outlet and can protect itself while growing from opposing creature deaths.

nonlands.name: Woe Strider
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Combines an outlet, an entry token, repeated scry, and escape-based recovery in one recurrable creature.

nonlands.name: Altar of Dementia
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: A free outlet that fuels graveyard recursion and can mill opponents or stock the deck's own graveyard without requiring mana.

nonlands.name: Ashnod's Altar
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Birthing Ritual is not a reliable sacrifice outlet; it only conditionally sacrifices at the end step. Ashnod's Altar is a free, repeatable outlet that converts Squirrels into mana and directly supports aristocrat turns without Pitiless Plunderer.

nonlands.name: Skullclamp
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: The premier way to turn 1/1 Squirrels and other expendable tokens into two cards each.

nonlands.name: Species Specialist
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Choosing Squirrel converts the deck's primary creature type into repeatable card draw whenever its board is sacrificed.

nonlands.name: Moldervine Reclamation
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Moldervine Reclamation draws whenever the deck's creatures die and gains life, directly rewarding Squirrel sacrifices and creature-based rebuilding. It is more aligned with the deck's primary sacrifice plan than relying mainly on creature entry.

nonlands.name: Beast Whisperer
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Turns the creature-dense ramp, token, outlet, and recursion shell into a steady stream of cards.

nonlands.name: Plumb the Forbidden
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Plumb the Forbidden converts a large token board into a substantial instant-speed refill and scales with multiple sacrifices, while also triggering the deck's death payoffs. This better supports post-wipe recovery and lethal aristocrat turns.

nonlands.name: Deadly Dispute
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Draws two cards while creating a Treasure, which Chatterfang and Manufactor turn into a much larger token event.

nonlands.name: Morbid Opportunist
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Provides dependable once-per-turn card draw from the frequent creature deaths generated by combat and sacrifice.

nonlands.name: Blood Artist
nonlands.primaryRole: Damage and life-total conversion from creature deaths
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: A cheap, efficient death payoff that converts every sacrificed Squirrel into damage and stabilizing life gain.

nonlands.name: Zulaport Cutthroat
nonlands.primaryRole: Damage and life-total conversion from creature deaths
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Its each-opponent drain makes a large finite sacrifice turn lethal across the table.

nonlands.name: Bastion of Remembrance
nonlands.primaryRole: Damage and life-total conversion from creature deaths
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Adds an initial Soldier and remains a resilient enchantment payoff that drains for every creature death.

nonlands.name: Mirkwood Bats
nonlands.primaryRole: Damage and life-total conversion from token creation and sacrifice
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Rewards both halves of the Chatterfang engine: creating tokens and sacrificing them, including artifact tokens from Manufactor.

nonlands.name: Poison-Tip Archer
nonlands.primaryRole: Damage and life-total conversion from creature deaths
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Adds another global death-drain effect while functioning as a useful defensive creature with reach and deathtouch.

nonlands.name: Nadier's Nightblade
nonlands.primaryRole: Damage and life-total conversion from tokens leaving the battlefield
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Triggers when Squirrels, Treasures, Clues, Foods, or other tokens leave, broadening the deck's drain redundancy.

nonlands.name: Marionette Apprentice
nonlands.primaryRole: Damage and life-total conversion from permanents entering the graveyard
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Fabricate supplies either a body or Servo, while every sacrificed creature or artifact adds another opponent-loss trigger.

nonlands.name: Assassin's Trophy
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Answers any opposing permanent type at instant speed, covering threats Chatterfang's -X/-X cannot handle.

nonlands.name: Abrupt Decay
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Efficiently answers most early engines and commanders while being uncounterable.

nonlands.name: Beast Within
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Removes any permanent and gives the opponent a Beast that can be managed or exploited as part of the token-focused plan.

nonlands.name: Nature's Claim
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: One-mana instant-speed coverage for the artifact and enchantment engines most likely to outscale this deck.

nonlands.name: Feed the Swarm
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Provides black access to enchantment removal while also answering creatures at low mana cost.

nonlands.name: Toxic Deluge
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: A scalable, low-cost sweeper that can clear larger creatures and preserve selected indestructible or noncreature engines.

nonlands.name: Force of Vigor
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Its alternate cost lets the deck interact through an opposing explosive turn without sacrificing development.

nonlands.name: Diabolic Intent
nonlands.primaryRole: Access to missing engine pieces or finishers
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Turns an expendable token into any needed engine, payoff, protection spell, or finisher while advancing the sacrifice plan.

nonlands.name: Finale of Devastation
nonlands.primaryRole: Access to creature engines and utility
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Finale retains creature-tutor access while also serving as a scalable win condition that grants a large team-wide pump and haste at high X. It increases access to engines and finishers without changing the fair, finite game plan.

nonlands.name: Chord of Calling
nonlands.primaryRole: Access to creature engines and finishers
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Convoke makes the token board a resource and permits instant-speed access to an outlet, payoff, protection creature, or finisher.

nonlands.name: Eternal Witness
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Returns any card, including a destroyed engine, tutor, protection spell, or finisher, while remaining creature-tutorable and recurrable.

nonlands.name: Victimize
nonlands.primaryRole: Recovery from board wipes and key-piece removal
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Exchanges a disposable token for two important creatures, rebuilding multiple engine pieces efficiently after disruption.

nonlands.name: Living Death
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Stocks the graveyard through sacrifice and milling, then returns a dense suite of creatures while forcing a table-wide creature exchange.

nonlands.name: Meren of Clan Nel Toth
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Meren supplies repeatable creature recursion, experience counters, and a creature body that can be found by the deck's tutors. It better exploits the sacrifice shell and improves recovery from targeted removal and sweepers than a single Regrowth.

nonlands.name: Heroic Intervention
nonlands.primaryRole: Protection for Chatterfang and critical engines
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Protects Chatterfang, token engines, payoffs, and lands from both targeted removal and most sweepers.

nonlands.name: Veil of Summer
nonlands.primaryRole: Protection for Chatterfang and critical engines
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Efficiently protects the engine from blue and black interaction while replacing itself when relevant.

nonlands.name: Tamiyo's Safekeeping
nonlands.primaryRole: Protection for Chatterfang and critical engines
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: A cheap protection spell for Chatterfang or a key permanent that also offsets the deck's life-payment costs.

nonlands.name: Craterhoof Behemoth
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: The strongest creature-based finisher for a wide Squirrel board and a premium target for Finale-like creature access effects.

nonlands.name: Triumph of the Hordes
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Ends games with a moderate board and costs substantially less than the largest creature finishers.

nonlands.name: Beastmaster Ascension
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: A low-cost permanent that quickly turns a token attack into a massive pump effect and remains useful over multiple combat steps.

nonlands.name: Scavenging Ooze
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Provides repeatable graveyard disruption while growing into a threat and improving life totals in sacrifice-heavy games.

nonlands.name: Soul-Guide Lantern
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Covers a graveyard card immediately, can exile an entire opposing graveyard, or replaces itself when the effect is unnecessary.

nonlands.name: Ygra, Eater of All
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Makes creatures into Foods that can be sacrificed, protects itself with Food, and grows rapidly as Food permanents reach the graveyard.

nonlands.name: The Meathook Massacre
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Combines scalable creature control with a durable death payoff that drains from the deck's own sacrifice waves.

nonlands.name: Evolutionary Leap
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Turns every expendable token into a creature card, increasing resilience and finding whichever creature role is missing.

nonlands.name: Mazirek, Kraul Death Priest
nonlands.whyInThisDeck: Turns the deck's creature, artifact, Clue, Food, and Treasure sacrifices into a large permanent team-wide power boost.

primaryWinPaths: Finite aristocrat finish: establish Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat, Bastion of Remembrance, Mirkwood Bats, Poison-Tip Archer, Nadier's Nightblade, or Marionette Apprentice alongside a sacrifice outlet and a substantial token board, then sacrifice tokens in waves for lethal drain.
Go-wide combat finish: develop a wide Squirrel and supporting-token board, then resolve Beastmaster Ascension, Triumph of the Hordes, or Craterhoof Behemoth and attack through blockers.

Resource-conversion finish: use Chatterfang, Manufactor, Tireless Provisioner, Skullclamp, and sacrifice outlets to convert token events into cards and mana until repeated drain triggers or a combat finisher becomes decisive.
secondaryWinPaths: Mazirek can turn a large sacrifice sequence into a lethal counter-enhanced attack even if aristocrat payoffs are absent.
Westvale Abbey can convert expendable creatures into Ormendahl as a resilient alternate combat threat.
The Meathook Massacre and Mirkwood Bats can close games through incremental token creation, sacrifice, and board control without requiring a single large attack.
constructedDeck.expectedPlayPattern: Use Forest-heavy opening hands to deploy one-mana creatures or Sol Ring, then cast efficient land ramp or an early token engine. Chatterfang is best cast when a token event is immediately available or when expendable Squirrels can fuel creature removal. In the midgame, maintain at least one outlet, one card engine, and one payoff while using tokens as cards, mana, removal, and protection from opposing attacks. Tutors find the missing creature or finisher rather than assembling a deterministic combo. After disruption, Eternal Witness, Victimize, Living Death, Regrowth, and creature-based engines rebuild the shell. Finish with a finite drain wave or a supported go-wide attack.
structuralNecessities: 36 lands with ten Forests and six Swamps to support early green ramp, black activated abilities, and basic-land resilience.
Nine early ramp and fixing cards to cast Chatterfang and three-to-five-mana engines on schedule.
Eight independent token engines, including both Squirrel producers and non-Squirrel artifact or creature token producers for Chatterfang conversion.
Six sacrifice outlets with multiple free or instant-speed options so token deaths can be converted into value on demand.
Seven card-advantage effects and seven aristocrat payoffs to sustain the board and make finite sacrifice turns lethal.
Seven flexible interaction spells covering permanents, sweepers, artifacts, enchantments, and graveyards.
Three moderate tutors, four recursion effects, and three protection spells to support resilience without creating a dedicated combo shell.
Three credible combat finishers that remain useful with a normal large token board.
The selected list avoids Pitiless Plunderer plus Ashnod's Altar and does not include any prohibited deterministic combo package.
